newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Pinochet will be out of town for Castro.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Pinochet will be out of town for Castro.

text.p: Former Chilean military ruler Augusto Pinochet, known for his blistering anti-communism, has arranged to be out of town when Cuban leader Fidel Castro comes to Chile on Saturday for a summit, the army said on Wednesday.
Pinochet and Air Force Commander Fernando Rojas will both be attending military exercises in northern Chile until Tuesday, the day after Castro leaves, military spokesmen said.
Rojas said recently he would rather not pay military honours to Castro at the Ibero-American Summit starting Sunday in Santiago, saying it "would not be agreeable."

"The general (Pinochet) will be out of Santiago attending military exercises for the next several days," said a spokesman. He did not know if Pinochet, 80, chose to attend the routine exercises to avoid having to meet Castro.

His absence will deprive the summit of what would have been one of its most interesting moments, a public shake-of-hands between Castro and Pinochet, seen by many Latin Americans as historic icons of the region's antagonistic left and right.

Pinochet, currently army commander-in-chief, and other Chilean military officers accuse Castro of arming and financing leftist guerrillas who wounded Pinochet in an assassination attempt in 1986. Thousands of communists were jailed, exiled or killed during Pinochet's 17-year-long military rule.
Castro's visit -- his first to Chile since 1971 when Marxist Salvador Allende was president -- has already become the summit's focus of attention three days before he even arrives.

Chile's main opposition party, the centre-right National Renewal, urged President Eduardo Frei's government on Wednesday to push for a resolution at the summit demanding democratic reforms to Cuba's one-party system.

"In Cuba there is no democracy and no respect for human rights. If our country has assumed a vocal position in defence of human rights and democracy, it should make that position known in this summit," said Andres Allamand, president of the party.

Chilean Communists planned welcome rallies and painted murals on outdoor walls extolling Castro, while Cuban exiles and local rightists planned protest rallies despite vows by Frei not to allow unauthorised demonstrations either for or against Castro.

Castro will be among 19 Latin American leaders attending the summit in Santiago on Sunday and the seaside city of Vina del Mar on Monday, as well as the prime ministers of Spain and Portugal and King Juan Carlos of Spain.
